reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently: web:Ps.45.0/1/9 dual-cite to oshb:Ps.45.1/2/10 correctly (Ps 45 is a shift+1 psalm per web_mt_offset_map.json, confirmed also by psalm_device_inventory.json mt_title_verses=[1]). Both Hebrew quotes in observed_substrate_signals collate at byte tier against verse_map_oshb.json (oshb:Ps.45.3, oshb:Ps.45.10 - checked via collate.collate_one, no shell transit). The genre-label claim (maskil, shir, bene-Qorach, al-shoshannim) matches psalm_device_inventory.json's genre_label_membership exactly (post-erratum figures). I independently read the full MT text of Ps.45.3-45.10 (all 8 verses): every visible pronominal suffix/verb form is 2ms (ש’פתותיך, ברכך at v3; חרבך at v4; והדרך/תורך/ימינך at v5; חציך/תחתיך at v6; כסאך/מלכותך at v7; אהבת/משחך/אלהיך/מחבריך at v8; בגדתיך/שמחוך at v9; ביקרותיך/לימינך at v10), so the underlying claim that address stays on the king through this span is TRUE. The span, the boundary at v9|v10 (verified via the 2fs shift at oshb:Ps.45.11, checked below under M8-Ps-128), the rejected_alternative, and confidence=high are all well-supported and I support them. My one challenge targets a narrower defect: campaign governance (TOOLKIT.md 'Standing rules' / book_strategy.md §10, sourced from Esth lesson b) requires every universal claim to carry an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its unit; check_universals.py independently flagged the same gap. See challenge LF-127-1.

challenges.claim: The row asserts a totalizing address-continuity claim twice ('continues without interruption' in rationale; 'stays fixed on the king throughout' in device_notes) without an adjacent digit-bearing count naming the swept unit, against the standing count-discipline rule.
challenges.evidence: device_notes: “this strophe’s address stays fixed on the king throughout”; rationale: “that continues without interruption” — neither clause is paired with a count. My own re-derivation confirms the claim is true but unswept: all 8 verses oshb:Ps.45.3-Ps.45.10 (=web:Ps.45.2-Ps.45.9) carry 2ms pronominal suffixes or verb forms with 0 exceptions, a count the row never states. check_universals.py independently flags the same 'throughout' phrase as an unswept universal claim.

reviews.reasoning: Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:45.10/15/17 = oshb:45.11/16/18, shift+1 rule). Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier (oshb:Ps.45.11, oshb:Ps.45.16). I independently checked the gender of every suffix from oshb:Ps.45.11 through oshb:Ps.45.16: v11 שִׁמְעִי/בַת/וּרְאִי (2fs imperative), אָזְנֵּךְ (2fs), עַמֵּךְ/אָבִיךְ (2fs) confirm the vocative shift to the bride at v11; the run of 2fs forms continues through v13 פָּנַיִךְ and v15 לָֽךְ ('brought to you', feminine לָךְ not masculine לְךָ, ruling out my initial concern that v14 WEB might re-address the king). Address reverts to masculine at oshb:Ps.45.17 אֲשֶֽׁךָ ('your fathers', 2ms), confirmed outside this row's own span, correctly placed as the NEXT row's opening signal. The strophe boundary (v9|v10 front seam, v15|v16 back seam) is driven by a genuine tier-1 addressee-gender shift on both ends, not selah or metadata. rejected_alternative is a single sentence, non-strawman, and correctly identifies the only plausible rival (extending through v17). confidence=high is warranted given the unambiguous grammatical marker.

Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:45.16/17 = oshb:45.17/18). The single Hebrew quote collates at byte tier (oshb:Ps.45.17). I independently confirmed the 2ms shift at oshb:Ps.45.17 אֲשֶֽׁךָ ('your fathers') resumes king-address after the 2fs bride-run of the prior strophe (verified under M8-Ps-128). Checked both absence claims against source inventories rather than trusting the row: pmarks_Ps.json shows zero selah/paseq/kq/reversednun/suspended entries anywhere in Ps 45, so 'no selah or other disclosure-object device' in this 2-verse span is TRUE and span-scoped correctly (also independently cleared by check_marks.py, 0 flags). The 'no doxology formula here' rejected_alternative claim is grounded in psalm_device_inventory.json's book_boundary_doxologies (only MT 41.14, 72.18-20, 89.53, 106.48 qualify; Book II runs 42-72 per five_books, so Ps 45 cannot structurally carry one) - this is tier-1 device-inventory grounding, not a bare tier-3/4 assertion. unit_type=strophe (not coda) is the correct controlled-vocabulary choice given book_strategy.md §6's definition of coda as doxology/colophon closes only. A 2-verse strophe is short relative to the §6 norm of ~4-8vv, but the addressee-shift driver at the front seam is decisive tier-1 evidence and I find no superior rival split; confidence=medium is a reasonable, non-overclaiming calibration given the unusually short span.

Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:46.0/1/3/7/11 = oshb:46.1/2/4/8/12, shift+1 rule). The Hebrew quote (oshb:Ps.46.2) collates at byte tier. Cross-checked the selah inventory directly: pmarks_Ps.json shows selah at oshb:Ps.46.4, 46.8, 46.12 only (3 occurrences, matching this row's own disclosure) - the row's claim that no refrain follows the v3/MT4 Selah, unlike the ones at v7/v11, is verified: MT.46.8 and MT.46.12 are byte-identical refrain verses (collate-checked directly against verse_map_oshb.json), while MT.46.4 (this row's closing verse) has no comparable refrain text before it. The genre labels (shir, bene-Qorach, al-alamot) match psalm_device_inventory.json's post-erratum genre_label_membership exactly (al_alamot={46} only, per the p02 erratum distinguishing it from Ps 9's almut-labben). unit_type=strophe (not refrain_unit) is the correct controlled-vocabulary distinction since this strophe's close carries selah without the refrain sentence, unlike the two rows that follow it. The 'missing initial refrain' crux is a real, debated scholarly question (Ps 46 is explicitly named as a refrain-lattice edge case); the row discloses it honestly without repairing the text or asserting a lost verse, and confidence=medium is the right calibration for a genuinely contested structural point. book_strategy.md §6 lists 46 among the refrain psalms where 'strophe rows follow the refrain returns' - this row matches the expected pattern.

Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:46.3/4/7/11 = oshb:46.4/5/8/12). Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier (oshb:Ps.46.5, oshb:Ps.46.8). I independently compared the full text of oshb:Ps.46.8 and oshb:Ps.46.12 and confirmed they are byte-identical (including the trailing Selah), corroborating the row's 'byte-identical across its 2 verse occurrences' claim - this is not merely trusted from the row but directly re-derived from verse_map_oshb.json. The topic pivot at oshb:Ps.46.5 (river/city of God, new image) versus the cosmic-upheaval imagery closing the prior strophe is confirmed from the Hebrew. unit_type=refrain_unit is a defensible, non-arbitrary application of the controlled vocabulary (whole_psalm|strophe|letter_stanza|refrain_unit|coda per book_strategy.md §6): this strophe's close IS refrain-corroborated, unlike the preceding strophe. device_notes correctly frames the refrain as corroboration and the topic shift as the actual driver, consistent with the policy that selah/refrain repetition is at most tier-3-like corroboration, never a driver alone. rejected_alternative (folding into one 6-verse unit) is a genuine, non-strawman rival, correctly rejected on the topic-shift evidence. confidence=high is warranted.

Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:46.7/8/11 = oshb:46.8/9/12). Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier (oshb:Ps.46.9, oshb:Ps.46.12). The imperative pair לְֽכוּ חֲזוּ at oshb:Ps.46.9 ('come, see') is a genuine 2mp imperative opening a new address, distinct in mood from the preceding report-and-refrain movement - verified directly from the Hebrew, not merely trusted. The refrain's second occurrence at oshb:Ps.46.12 was already confirmed byte-identical to oshb:Ps.46.8 under M8-Ps-131. unit_type=refrain_unit is consistently applied for the same reason as the preceding row (refrain-corroborated close). The rejected_alternative (folding into one 8-verse unit) is a fair rival, rejected on the mood/address-shift evidence at the imperative opening, which is the strongest available driver. This row closes the psalm exactly at oshb:Ps.46.12, so no further seam question arises past its end. confidence=high is warranted; tiling for all of Ps 46 (rows 130-132) is exact with no gaps or overlaps (check_tiling.py, GREEN).

Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:47.0/1/4 = oshb:47.1/2/5; the cross-psalm context ref web:46.11=oshb:46.12 also checks out and is correctly disclaimed in-row as context, not boundary evidence for THIS psalm - it does not cross this row's own span, which stays entirely inside Ps 47, satisfying the 'rows never cross psalm boundaries' rule). I read the full MT text of Ps.47.2-47.5 to test the rationale's claim that the imperative summons 'continues to govern the psalm's stance... without a new address' through the Selah: v3/MT (כִּֽי יְהוָה...) is a 3rd-person motive clause (grounds for the summons, standard call+motive psalm rhetoric, no new addressee), and v4-5/MT (יַדְבֵּר.../יִבְחַר...) continue the same motive with 1cp suffixes ('under us', 'for us') rather than addressing a new party - the rejected_alternative (splitting after the reason clause at v2/MT.47.3) is correctly rejected since no addressee change occurs there. Genre labels (mizmor, bene-Qorach) match psalm_device_inventory.json exactly. confidence=high is warranted; the opening title dual-cite (web:Ps.47.0=oshb:Ps.47.1) is correctly present per the titled-psalm opening-row rule.

Dual-cite arithmetic verified (web:47.5/6/8/9 = oshb:47.6/7/9/10). Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier (oshb:Ps.47.6, oshb:Ps.47.7). I independently counted the imperative זַמְּרוּ/זַמֵּּרוּ in oshb:Ps.47.7: it occurs exactly 4 times within that single verse, matching the row's digit-bearing claim ('occurs four times within one verse') and correctly naming its unit. This strophe runs from the narrative report of the ascent through the psalm's final verse, so the back seam is fixed by the psalm's own end and needs no independent seam argument. The row's chosen internal grouping (report + imperative cluster + declaration as one strophe, mirroring the summons+reason+report+Selah shape of the preceding strophe) is a coherent, defensible bipartite reading of Ps 47 and the rejected_alternative (a split before the imperative cluster) is a genuine, non-strawman rival correctly rejected on the shared-scene argument; I found no decisive tier-1 counter-evidence for a stronger rival split. device_notes correctly distinguishes this strophe's climax from a book-boundary doxology, consistent with psalm_device_inventory.json (Ps 47 does not appear among the four doxology seams). confidence=high is warranted.
